correctness.rationale: For every even integer d>=4 and every matching with k<d, graph-state entropy is binary biadjacency rank. The group-algebra nilpotent computation gives rank(B)=2^(d-2). The original Key–Seneviratne theorem gives minimum nonzero weight d in im A_d, forcing matching endpoint independence modulo image and coimage. The proved rank-update lemma yields +k. A full kernel computation gives r+d-1 for the all-neighbor matching, while a replacement endpoint removes the unique quotient dependence to give r+d. Every quantifier and the sharpness boundary are explicit. Integer GF2 checker directly computed 4031 finite ranks as corroboration, not proof.

value.rationale: Arbitrary vertex-disjoint CZ omissions form a natural, physically interpretable ideal preparation-fault family. A sharp all-placement threshold tied to code distance, accompanied by constructive first placement bifurcation, is a complete structural rule rather than a routine numerical invariant. The counterexample at k=d shows why an additive extrapolation beyond the threshold is false.
